sentences.text: Solicitor Helen Moss attended the meeting with client Gareth Pryce.
The purpose of the meeting was to discuss Gareth Pryce's mother's estate, specifically the house on Wyvern Road.
Gareth Pryce's mother died in June.
The house on Wyvern Road was left to Gareth and his brother Neil in equal shares, 50-50.
There is a will naming both Gareth and Neil as executors.
Probate has not yet been applied for.
Neil is living in the house and refuses to move out.
An estate agent provided an estimated valuation of £280,000 for the house.
Neil refused to allow a proper valuation by an estate agent.
Gareth and Neil have a strained relationship, described as 'bad' or 'really bad'.
On Saturday, 7th November, Neil punched Gareth in the face during an argument in the kitchen about the sale of the house.
Gareth's nose was broken during the incident, and he was taken to hospital that night.
Gareth was treated at Castlebrook General Hospital A and E, where an x-ray confirmed a broken nose.
After being punched, Gareth was on the floor and was hit in the back and shoulder with a kitchen chair.
Gareth had bruising down his back for a week following the incident.
Gareth stated that Neil was 'like a different person' during the incident.
Gareth said he did not believe Neil had a knife or picked one up during the incident, but that he was angry and it scared him.
Gareth left the house after getting up and walking out, then drove himself to hospital.
Gareth has not reported the incident to the police.
Gareth said he is thinking about reporting the incident to the police, but is concerned about his mother's feelings.
Gareth has a discharge letter from Castlebrook General Hospital.
Gareth took photos of his face the day after the incident.
Neil has sent texts to Gareth, saying he 'deserved it' and that he is not getting a penny.
Gareth wants the house sold and the estate settled.
Gareth wants Neil to stay away from him.
As joint executors, both Gareth and Neil must act to apply for probate, but if Neil refuses to cooperate, the solicitor advised that a court application to remove Neil as an execu­
The solicitor advised that a letter to Neil should be written, setting out a deadline, and that Gareth should consider reporting the assault to the police.
The solicitor advised that a non-molestation order could be applied for in family court to prevent Neil from contacting or approaching Gareth.
The solicitor stated that a non-molestation order could be processed quickly if urgent.
The solicitor will send a client care letter with fees by Friday.
